senses.gloss:
lobha
(‘greed’)
------------------------------------------
All religions in general and हिन्दुइस्म् in particular, stress the importance of cultivating some basic ethical principles. One of these is eschewing greed.
‘Lobha,’ translated as ‘greed’, is excessive desire, especially the desire to appropriate to oneself what belongs to others; that too, against the principles of धर्म.
The Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad in its very first verse advises us not to covet anyone’s wealth and possessions. The Bhagavadgītā (16.21) calls it as a gateway to हेल्ल् and exhorts the aspirant to give it up.
Lobha is classed among the ariṣaḍ-vargas or six enemies of man, the others being काम (lust), krodha (anger), मोह (infatuation), मद (intoxication) and mātsarya (jealousy).
